title: §03-002: Closure Mechanics & Parallel Closures
description: Multiple-choice practice questions and deep runtime verification for §03-002 (Closure Mechanics & Parallel Closures).

cards.concept: Closure Mechanics & Parallel Closures: Closure Memory Retention & Heap Allocation
cards.question: How does V8 preserve outer lexical scope bindings captured by an inner closure that outlives its parent function?

options.text: It duplicates the entire process memory space to worker threads.
V8 allocates a Context object on the managed Heap to store captured variables, referenced via the inner function's internal [[Scopes]] link.
It serializes the scope into JSON buffers in the code cache.
It locks the operating system thread from terminating.

cards.explanation: When variables in an outer function are captured by an escaping inner function, V8 allocates a Heap Context for those variables. The inner function retains a reference via its internal [[Scopes]] property.
cards.pitfall: Capturing large objects or buffers in an outer scope that is referenced by a long-lived closure (e.g. interval callback) prevents GC reclamation, creating a memory leak.
cards.citation: V8 Internals Documentation / Node.js Memory Management Guide

cards.concept: Closure Mechanics & Parallel Closures: Private Class Fields vs Closure Encapsulation
cards.question: How do ECMAScript Private Class Fields (`#field`) guarantee hard encapsulation compared to closure-based private variables?

options.text: Private fields are stored in global Symbol registries accessible via getOwnPropertySymbols.
Private fields use internal private brand checks enforced at bytecode level; they cannot be accessed or overridden outside class declaration.
Private fields are encrypted using AES-256 in memory.
Private fields create a new V8 heap isolate per class instance.

cards.explanation: Private class fields (#field) provide hard private state. Outside code cannot inspect or access them even with Object.getOwnPropertyNames or Proxy reflection.
cards.pitfall: Attempting to dynamically access private fields using bracket notation (this[`#${name}`]) is a syntax error.
cards.citation: MDN Web Docs: Private properties / TC39 Class Fields Proposal
